notes.title: Update 1.9.1
notes.content: [p][b]Hello everyone![/b][/p][p]This update is a bit out of schedule. Some survey results pointed to you guys wanting a more alternating release cycle, so here is a small patch for you to enjoy![/p][p]I also wanted to gather some feedback and performance analysis for the new graphical features instead of releasing a big patch with everything broken. Saves me headaches later, makes you happy earlier. Win-win situation right here.[/p][p]However, let’s not make the intro longer than the patch notes, so let’s get to it![/p][p][/p][h1]New Volumetrics[/h1][p]The last patch introduced a bunch of details to our beloved snowy tundra, and this update aims to take visual fidelity further across all available maps.[/p][p]Here is a before and after for each map:[/p][p][/p][h3]Capital Outskirts[/h3][p]before[/p][p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45228567/b4615b26507c486b1cda6f64e98f8d2a9aafb7d6.jpg"][/img][/p][p]after[/p][p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45228567/048fea4d56a902e9d32dcc32ec39f8135103838f.jpg"][/img][/p][h3]Tundra of the North[/h3][p]before[/p][p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45228567/c1aab0f22bb473a0e8bb8e196e3da232b2c79fbe.jpg"][/img][/p][p]after[/p][h3][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45228567/a836bd3485b85d1965b279eac202b1e03137ebbf.jpg"][/img][/h3][h3]Underground Dungeons[/h3][p]before[/p][p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45228567/86c39f56f1261c426c47f41dc926ecd6ab1a03e1.jpg"][/img][/p][p]after[/p][p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45228567/0a9dda1df720a9abe44433ee51c5f870908d1f8e.jpg"][/img][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45228567/6622050d316e25f33856fbffb1ff2966bdf35663.jpg"][/img][/p][p]By default, right after the update, the quality of volumetric effects will be set fairly low to avoid issues on lower-end devices.[/p][p]Regardless, I encourage you to try setting these options higher and report back with the results.[/p][p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45228567/43e9211f357eb427be63984872a18ebd1bcade5e.jpg"][/img][/p][p]For snow map you also need a [i]Far [/i]render distance to render clouds in the sky.[/p][p]My 3080 runs a fairly stable 100+ fps with quality settings maxed out, but I’d like to get some feedback from a wider variety of hardware to make sure it performs well enough![/p][p][/p][h1]Performance Optimizations[/h1][p]The Capital Outskirts map can be quite resource-intensive with settings cranked up, but this version should improve performance for trees and [i]3D+[/i] grass rendering. As a result, foliage may look a bit less bushy, but the optimizations allow for higher [i]instanced[/i] grass density at the same performance cost.[/p][p]Just don’t go overboard with grass density if you want to keep over 60 fps![/p][p][/p][p]The Tundra of the North map should also run slightly better on high snow settings.[/p][p][/p][h1]Underground Dungeons Rework[/h1][p]As you may have noticed from the comparison screenshots, the dungeon (aside from ambient lighting) looks quite different.[/p][p]That’s because the map has been completely remade![/p][p]It’s not fully complete yet. It has all the features the previous one had, but is still missing some decorations. These will come in a future update.[/p][p]The layout is similar to the old one but much more diverse.[/p][p]Here are a few screenshots for your viewing pleasure:[/p][p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45228567/d555eb061305ea95922a36bf07c483f3ff3c0da3.jpg"][/img][/p][p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45228567/3cb810124306ef0022cd6708f574db2d63cb6b6f.jpg"][/img][/p][p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45228567/40a85afcc6aa9e18695c3164992e58fd8bcca196.jpg"][/img][/p][p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45228567/fcb0a1b4a8ecaada5ef32ff4dfc2e188ae9976e3.jpg"][/img][/p][p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45228567/c7fece14acced58fe562a2080a253d69eb9c964f.jpg"][/img][/p][p]Not so much “Underground Dungeons” anymore, so it might need a rebranding. [/p][p][/p][h2]Top-Down View[/h2][p]The top-down camera was also adjusted to “work” with this map, though some rooms still won’t cooperate due to current technical limitations.[/p][p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45228567/f28f21895abffdb0a47a5e1f29e512da98b95b4d.jpg"][/img][/p][h1]Relic Loadouts[/h1][p]A while back I saw a request to unify relic pages in one of the survey reports.[/p][p]That did go against the design choice I made when initially implementing relics, but I found a way to implement it that should satisfy everyone.[/p][p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45228567/9e7fa675e761ce356a7ad77ca93ebacc48c90ea7.jpg"][/img]Loadouts replaced the previous [i]Recommendations[/i] tab and can be accessed from the toolbar.[/p][p]You can create as many loadouts as you want, name them, set relic priorities, limits, and so on, then apply everything with a single click.[/p][p]You can even make the system reuse relics from other characters (though it will unequip relics from those characters).[/p][p]All the advanced settings are accessible by clicking the hamburger button on the top right.[/p][p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45228567/7e9d9e14d335508be56dd03ad866add959625876.jpg"][/img][/p][p]You can create a loadout from the currently active relic page by selecting the [i]New From Equipped[/i] option.[/p][p]You can even export your current loadout into a file to share with others![/p][p][/p][h2]Loadout Editing[/h2][p]When editing or adding a new relic to the loadout, you can set a limit for the maximum value of a stat.[/p][p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45228567/015aa32e96f8854727411cff7a2dfbf85934279b.jpg"][/img][/p][h2]How does it work?[/h2][p]The inner workings are pretty simple. First, prepare a list of relics you want automatically equipped.[/p][p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45228567/fddff3c37e18b967c84c00112876a9b25fa1498a.jpg"][/img][/p][p][/p][p]Relics at the top will take priority over those below. In the example above, the Crit Rate relic is at the very top of the list with a limit set to 35%.[/p][p]The system will equip relics into every [i]Offense[/i] and [i]Mixed[/i] slot until the combined bonuses reach 35%. Once the 35% crit rate is reached, the remaining [i]Offense[/i] and [i]Mixed[/i] slots will be filled with the [i]Crit Damage[/i] relic defined below.[/p][p]Then all the [i]Defensive[/i] and remaining [i]Mixed[/i] slots will be filled with the [i]Health Regen[/i] relics, and so on.[/p][p]You can change the order of relics by simply dragging them around.[/p][p][/p][h1]Character Tuner Details[/h1][p]Following the previous update, Character Tuner is now getting the missing feature of viewing weapon details.[/p][p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45228567/0aa7fbdce2dca8e3383e788f5c512d6676f1a3e8.jpg"][/img][/p][p]Hover over an item currently used in your build to expand it. You can view the full description and basic weapon stats such as damage dealt.[/p][p]You can also adjust weapon level to see how different upgrades affect stats with each level unlocked, as well as view what each upgrade does at every level.[/p][p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45228567/43782b48f1cf83968848aaeb2b3637b69e56ef62.jpg"][/img][/p][p]I couldn’t implement the details into the main item list due to technical limitations, but I hope this is enough (┬┬﹏┬┬)[/p][p][/p][h1]Changes not mentioned in 1.9[/h1][p]I did comment on these under the last post, but I’ll also mention them here.[/p][h2]Enemy knockback[/h2][p]Enemies now take knockback from various attacks. It’s been on my backlog for a long time and I wish I had implemented it sooner. Anyway, it made it into 1.9 without testing (with another hotfix patch), so... yeah.[/p][h2]Pierce projectiles[/h2][p]Another change that slipped into 1.9 is how piercing projectiles behave. I felt they fell short compared to AoE types. With the introduction of knockback, they became much more powerful, but still not quite where I’d like them.[/p][p]Previously, pierce projectiles internally kept a count of how many enemies they [i]touched[/i]. If the counter exceeded the projectile’s [i]pierce count[/i] stat, the projectile would despawn.[/p][p]This had a few flaws.[/p][p]Firstly, projectiles couldn’t damage multiple enemies even if it looked like they did, because once the pierce count was exceeded, the damage was nullified. Each pierce could only deal one instance of damage and that was it.[/p][p]With the changes, the internal counter increments once the projectile [i]leaves[/i] an enemy collider, allowing it to deal damage to groups of enemies. Hitting 5 enemies will still consume 5 counts of pierce, but now it will also deal 5 instances of damage, even if the pierce count for the projectile is just 2.[/p][p]Another change (that started as a bug): pierce count is no longer consumed if the target dies.[/p][p]So yeah, that was a bug I encountered while testing the previous change, but I figured it felt pretty good and made sense, so I kept it. Now pierce projectiles can pierce unlimited targets as long as they die in a single tick of damage.[/p][p][/p][h1]Bug Fixes[/h1][list][*][p]The character screen displayed an incorrect max count for relics[/p][/*][*][p]When opening Character Tuner for the first time, the default weapon should have been added automatically. However, it wouldn’t be saved and the first slot of the build would get locked.[/p][/*][/list][p][/p][h1]Launch issues after update[/h1][p]Following a thread that mentioned antivirus software flagging version 1.9 for whatever reason: if you have trouble running the game after the update, please let me know. I’ve had one report that seemed to resolve itself, but I’m curious if there are any other cases.[/p][p]Could be a one-off case, could be a wider issue — I wouldn’t want people getting locked out like that.[/p][p][/p][h1]Le Tease[/h1][p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45228567/60c2636de9f82009e39df49bf69848e39267d7c9.jpg"][/img][/p][p]Just so you know, I’ve already started working on the next map. I hope you fw deserts![/p][p][/p][h1]Afterword[/h1][p]That’s it for the changes.[/p][p]I had two weeks off work and decided to cram in as many features as I could during that time. [/p][p]Needless to say, I got no rest done, but at least the results are quite satisfactory to me (●'◡'●).[/p][p]I also tallied up the overall cost of development, and man, I spent way more than I initially intended. I blame Unity for that tho. It’s a decent game engine, but the amount of missing features is baffling, and filling in the gaps gets expensive quickly. Anyway, just a rant on my part![/p][p]The next update most likely won’t be out too soon. I’ll be back to my 9-5, and the upcoming features will be time-consuming to implement (Clara, new enemies, and the new map). Regardless, I hope you’ll stick around when the time comes :D[/p][p][/p][p]Once again, thank you to everyone who continues to support the game (even quietly by just playing). It keeps me motivated to open the project each day![/p][p]Also, if you enjoy Requiem For a Lost World, please share it around as it helps massively, leave a positive review too. Or if you’re familiar with advertising, hit me up.[/p][p]I’m extremely bad at getting this game out there o(TヘTo)[/p][p][/p]

notes.title: Version Update 1.9.0
notes.content: [p]Hello everyone![/p][p][/p][p]Today is a good day for an update, or so I hope![/p][p]I'm super excited to finally release it—1.9 has been in the works for what feels like an eternity. Working with a vague deadline has been pretty nice; it allowed me to work on stuff at my own pace without having to cut corners on some features just to push anything out.[/p][p]I also feel that working when I actually feel like it provides much better results.[/p][p]But enough yapping, we have stuff to show off! I've prepared a list that I hope is fairly complete, but it's unorganized, so bear with me if the following may be a bit messy. ┗( T﹏T )┛[/p][p][/p][p]Aaaaanyway, grab some snacks; it will be a long read![/p][p][/p][h1]New Character[/h1][p]Let's get the first thing out of the way, which is the new character I teased a couple of days ago.[/p][p][/p][h2][b]Nishi - The Duskbringer[/b][/h2][p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45228567/7ece36e1b676f4977fc22ecfcc7a3bf1460f6e79.png"][/img][/p][p]As per usual, let us go over the kit and some design decisions.[/p][p]The Duskbringer does not have his own archetype; as such, you can build him however you want. [i]We are going back to the roots with this one![/i][/p][p][/p][p]His signature weapon, [b]Divine Judgement[/b],[b] [/b]is an AoE Light-type weapon summoning down divine swords from above.[/p][p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45228567/5b904633d2edce21a7623f61bf534d4f275249ff.gif"][/img][/p][p]But since his weapon is nothing special and his kit does not reward a specific archetype, isn't he just a simple DPS character?[/p][p]Well, his ultimate is what makes him stand out! [b]Until I Save You [/b]is an ability that allows Nishi to turn back time while retaining part of the power obtained before the time has been reset.[/p][p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45228567/614a0797e5e10e88b7f4293e23aa6267b2c4cb10.gif"][/img][/p][p]Now a few notes on this ability since it ties to his passive. Whenever Nishi enters the Memory Rift (the boss drop), he will obtain a [i]Core[/i]. When he owns at least 5 Cores, the ultimate can be used to reset the stage timer, acquired weapons, items, gold, and gems in exchange for [i]Elemental Damage[/i] and [i]Elemental Cooldown[/i] buffs depending on the number of Cores owned before the reset. [/p][p]You can read the in-game description to learn more![/p][hr][/hr][p]Now, as per usual, let us get into some design decisions! [/p][p]I wanted to make a character that felt unique in terms of gameplay loop. New characters tend to come out with a new gimmick: Natalie introduced DoT, Mucha made it crit, Amelisana innovated the way I do passives, Nyxaria introduced Elemental Accumulations, and so on. I went back and forth between wanting the last form of Nishi to be playable or not, but the kind of kit I had in my head was just too perfect for him: a character able to grow stronger indefinitely. So I went ahead and tied his kit to the story, and I think it turned out quite well, from the collection of Cores to the screen fade with text into a new cycle. The journey is also reflected on the shards, but the text itself won't be available to read until I'm done with all the other characters.[/p][p]I fully expect the leaderboard to become a complete mess because of him, but we'll see how it goes.[/p][p][/p][h1]Character Reworks[/h1][p]As announced earlier, I started working on the older characters to step away from the traditional "level-up increases" into something more interactive. In version 1.9, two characters got their kits reworked.[/p][p][/p][h2]Adam [/h2][p]Adam was one of the first characters introduced into Requiem For a Lost World back in 2023.[/p][p]He was supposed to fit into the role of a farming character, allowing players to gather currency more effectively, and it worked back then. I wanted to keep his function while bringing his kit up to more modern standards.[/p][p]Adam will now properly scale with [b]Luck[/b] and [b]Greed[/b] stats, allowing him to build into his original farming role while retaining enough damage to actually clear stages.[/p][p][/p][h2]Chitose[/h2][p]I always kept Chitose in mind as this lively girl running and dashing around. However, the gameplay did not reflect that.[/p][p]In the spirit of the original idea behind her, she will now properly scale with movement-based stats. She also got her own [i]Special[/i] bar that can be filled by dashing or sprinting and provides additional bonuses once full.[/p][p][b]Chitose will now be available as a starting character for new and existing players.[/b][/p][p][/p][h1]New Weapons[/h1][p]We've got plenty of different weapons in the game, but it doesn't hurt to add more![/p][p]There are 9 new weapons and 1 new item.[/p][p]I won't go into big details here (this changelog is long enough as it is).[/p][p]These new weapons focus on either dealing heavy damage infrequently or empowering elemental reactions! [/p][p]Read the rest of the changes and go check them out![/p][p][/p][h1]New Elemental Reactions[/h1][p]Speaking of empowering elemental reactions. Here are a few new ones for you all to trigger~[/p][list][*][p]Quanta ([b]Cosmic [/b]+ [b]Lightning[/b])[/p][list][*][p]Enemies take 100% more damage; additionally, deal an instance of damage if the enemy has a Lightning weakness equal to 200% of damage dealt.[/p][/*][/list][/*][*][p]Dilation ([b]Cosmic [/b]+ [b]Ice[/b])[/p][list][*][p]Apply ice-type DoT equal to 50% of damage dealt every 0.5s for 3 seconds.[/p][/*][/list][/*][*][p]Corruption ([b]Cosmic[/b] + [b]Dark[/b])[/p][list][*][p]Deal a random instance of damage between 100% and 1000% of damage dealt.[/p][/*][/list][/*][*][p]Dilation ([b]Cosmic [/b]+ [b]Ice[/b])[/p][list][*][p]Apply ice-type DoT equal to 50% of damage dealt every 0.5s for 3 seconds.[/p][/*][/list][/*][*][p]Blessing ([b]Light[/b] + [b]Wind[/b])[/p][list][*][p]Heal all player characters for 10% of damage dealt.[/p][/*][/list][/*][*][p]Invigorated ([b]Light[/b] + [b]Fire[/b])[/p][list][*][p]Increase damage dealt by all player characters by 30% for 2 seconds.[/p][/*][/list][/*][/list][p]As you may have noticed, there are plenty of new cosmic-related reactions. [/p][p]I always intended the Cosmic element to be reaction-focused. Yami-no-Tokiya boosts elemental reaction effects, Nyxaria heavily implants Cosmic onto enemies, and even Cosmic accumulation boosts elemental reaction effects. But Cosmic itself had no useful reactions, especially since RES PEN was introduced. As a result, you would never build Cosmic to do reaction-based damage.[/p][p]So it's time to change that. With the new reactions, you can build Cosmic and deal major reaction damage in one go![/p][p][/p][h1]Elemental Resonance[/h1][p]Let's continue pushing the elemental topic, shall we?[/p][p]Version 1.9 introduces a new elemental mechanic that favors single- or dual-element builds.[/p][p]Elemental Resonance activates after a player obtains three weapons of the same element. Different elements will provide different effects; some of these effects get stronger the more weapons of that element are equipped. [/p][p]So players can choose between running mono element for increased benefits or dual element to activate two Elemental Resonances at the same time.[/p][p]As of version 1.9, the following effects can be triggered:[/p][list][*][p]Fire Resonance[/p][list][*][p]Increases health and damage dealt.[/p][/*][/list][/*][*][p]Lightning Resonance[/p][list][*][p]A low chance to trigger an additional projectile with each attack; the chance increases with the number of Lightning weapons equipped.[/p][/*][/list][/*][*][p]Ice Resonance[/p][list][*][p]A high chance to deal additional damage; the additional damage increases with the number of Ice weapons equipped.[/p][/*][/list][/*][*][p]Physical Resonance[/p][list][*][p]Increases crit damage and crit rate.[/p][/*][/list][/*][*][p]Wind Resonance[/p][list][*][p]Increases stamina regeneration, movement speed, and DoT dealt.[/p][/*][/list][/*][*][p]Light Resonance[/p][list][*][p]Increases healing effects and shard pull distance. Additionally, kills have a chance to spawn a light orb that grants EXP, gold, and gems on pickup.[/p][/*][/list][/*][*][p]Cosmic Resonance[/p][list][*][p]Team-wide elemental effect increase and all-type RES PEN.[/p][/*][/list][/*][*][p]Earth Resonance[/p][list][*][p]Generates a shield over time; the shield charges faster the more Earth weapons are owned.[/p][/*][/list][/*][*][p]Dark Resonance[/p][list][*][p]Grants flat healing per hit and additional life steal.[/p][/*][/list][/*][/list][p]I hope this will be an interesting mechanic for you all to mess around with![/p][p][/p][h1]Northern Tundra Map Overhaul[/h1][p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45228567/33487bdbda20101ca23fa749d868027ae1724ae2.jpg"][/img][/p][p]Ever since the release of this map I felt like it was lacking in the visual department (snow tracks didn't pull their weight). So as part of 1.9, I went ahead and added some detail to the map:[/p][list][*][p]New trees[/p][/*][*][p]Rocky mountains[/p][/*][*][p]Overhangs[/p][/*][*][p]Frozen Lakes[/p][/*][/list][p]Just to name a few![/p][p][/p][h1]Power Monoliths[/h1][p]While on the topic of maps, let me quickly introduce new rocks that will spawn around the Capital Outskirts and Northern Tundra.[/p][p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45228567/bb3704109e602d7f969947b88373651164ae6f0d.jpg"][/img][/p][p]You can interact with them during gameplay to obtain stat increases that last until the end of the run (or time rewind). [/p][p]A limited number of them will spawn around the map, but they can be activated multiple times after a set cooldown, of course.[/p][p][/p][h1]Tutorial Stage[/h1][p]A new tutorial stage will be available, introducing the game's basic mechanics.[/p][p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45228567/f9829ac2d4b8a30e38bacf1a1112b36200e30928.jpg"][/img][/p][p]Initially I added a bunch of tips on the screen during normal gameplay, but later I figured a dedicated tutorial stage would probably be a better decision.[/p][p]The tutorial will explain how elements, combat, and leveling up work.[/p][p][/p][h1]UI Stuff[/h1][p]As per usual, the update will also bring a few changes to the UI.[/p][p][/p][h2]New Shard Graphics[/h2][p]As mentioned in my previous post, I spent a substantial amount of time redoing every shard graphic for each character to get rid of the signature AI-generated look. I will let you all decide if it's an improvement![/p][p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45228567/85b7968c609d4ef5f6451a67e2c985f3882f1648.jpg"][/img][/p][p]You can also inspect each one by clicking the little magnifying glass or pressing the [i]Enter[/i] key while highlighting a shard.[/p][p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45228567/507621d148328ca4a9a48ebae576627889219a0b.jpg"][/img][/p][h2]New Character Cards[/h2][p]Alongside the shards, I also updated all the character cards to match the same style.[/p][p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45228567/de0cb86c88f02e4dc2e9240594cd311208c40dce.jpg"][/img][/p][p]The cards are not 100% finished and will be gradually improved over time as well![/p][p][/p][p]While we are here, a quick change to the character selection screen: [/p][list][*][p]The passive box is now bigger to show more of the passive description.[/p][/*][*][p]The stat view has been simplified to show only the essential stats.[/p][/*][/list][p][/p][h2]New Character Tuner UI[/h2][p]I confess I put the previous Tuner interface in as a last-minute requested feature and have hated it ever since.[/p][p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45228567/5056d6c97afd19436f50ea66d7a9dc379546975a.jpg"][/img][/p][p]I finally got around to doing it properly this time. You can switch between weapons and items, filter them based on element, and see the summarized description right there on the screen.[/p][p]A more detailed view will come later once I figure out exactly how I want it to look.[/p][p][/p][h2]Improved Leaderboard UI[/h2][p]It's a small change.[/p][p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45228567/9df9ec4b63f8d3debad6cf4304f0b86cc1db5746.jpg"][/img][/p][p]You can't see it on the screenshot since only new scores will have it, so you have to trust me on this. [/p][p]The leaderboard will now display the player's name card on the entry as well[/p][p]This is the name card, btw:[/p][p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45228567/6ecca4b98a0a42f9ab52ecd1b06b7e472e3f7b5f.jpg"][/img][/p][p]And top scores now glow a bit.[/p][p][/p][h2]New Name Cards[/h2][p]A little bit of a side quest while we are on the topic. [/p][p]I've added a few new name cards to the game with plans to add even more in the upcoming versions![/p][p]Here is one of them[/p][p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45228567/b3ae5d2f8333cfef26dc2bca33501003a6adc05a.png"][/img][/p][p][/p][h2]New Recollection UI and Rules[/h2][p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45228567/39677e6781def12c3aebab7c21e5054f22b2cc3c.jpg"][/img][/p][p]So I also touched the Recollection UI. It's not like I had anything against the old one, but I decided to get it up to the standards as well.[/p][p]The new screen now displays the kit overview for the current banner character, including all the rank-up buffs as well.[/p][p]The previous three additional boosted characters are now gone and replaced with additional banners. Players can now choose which character they want to pull for from the three active banners.[/p][p]So as we all know, the gacha in Requiem For a Lost World is purely for fun, and the rates guarantee you a character or couple with each 10 pull. [/p][p]But if you are masochistic, I've also added an option for you:[/p][p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45228567/dbe2166d073bca41890453b02c3a9758154b670e.jpg"][/img][/p][p]This is of course off by default, but if you crave the [i]real[/i] gacha experience, then this is for you —it lowers the rates to current standards (0.6% for the main character and 5% for side characters respectively).[/p][p]Do with this option as you please.[/p][p][/p][h2]Improved Result Screen UI[/h2][p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45228567/ef2df48ffc142aaa8ff8f622a383b81559e5b102.png"][/img][/p][p]A few new stats are being displayed at the summary:[/p][list][*][p]Elemental Reaction trigger count[/p][/*][*][p]Elemental Infliction trigger count[/p][/*][*][p]Total damage taken[/p][/*][*][p]Total healing received[/p][/*][/list][p]The damage summary will now also display decimal places because precision is important.[/p][p]The weapon damage summary will now also display DPS on top of total damage dealt.[/p][p]There is also a toggle for [i]Effective Damage[/i], but we will get into that later.[/p][p][/p][h2]Improved Level Up UI [/h2][p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45228567/bcebb0a87ac5e9af5ffef08c3fe7bc133dfac35d.jpg"][/img][/p][p]When leveling up, players will be able to see basic weapon stats such as damage dealt (non-crit and crit), attack cooldown, and projectile duration. If the upgrade changes any of these stats, the change will also be displayed.[/p][p]In addition to stat display, weapons that don't scale with attack count, size, or duration increase will also get an appropriate indicator.[/p][h2][/h2][h2]New Pause Screen UI[/h2][p]This is a big one, so buckle up.[/p][p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45228567/1c297704e83ba3921c08a1362ab9474a6a337d35.jpg"][/img][/p][p]The new pause screen displays way more information now. Including active effects coming from weapons, skills, or other players. [/p][p]Similar to the character selection screen, the stats have been simplified but you can view the full list by clicking the magnifying glass button.[/p][p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45228567/d1ea9669a3e8a1e1a111852aa158da78cbbea2b7.jpg"][/img][/p][p]This window displays all stats, including hidden stats unavailable for viewing before. [/p][p]You can filter stats by searching up the name. The new stat system that we will touch upon in a bit allows for per-element boosts, and that menu also accommodates those.[/p][p]But that's not all the pause screen provides.[/p][p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45228567/324a907e54f3610263cefcfb0355426dcd50d5ec.jpg"][/img][/p][p]When hovering over a weapon or item, a summary will be displayed, including current stats and total damage/damage contributed by this weapon.[/p][p]The weapon bar can be toggled between weapons and items by clicking the icon above it.[/p][p]To top it all off, you can toggle the stats and kit display to view a character's kit in case you forgot what they do.[/p][p][/p][h2]Relic Page Stats UI[/h2][p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45228567/67a389587e7c2b73935873ec182a088c9abb87c4.jpg"][/img][/p][p]In the same fashion as the pause screen, you can view stats modified by equipped relics.[/p][p][/p][h2]Low Health Indication[/h2][p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45228567/49355256048580e3657d564f287147f26b513b4e.jpg"][/img][/p][p]When health becomes low, the world will start losing colors, and only red hues will remain. This can be toggled in settings.[/p][p][/p][h1]New Stats System[/h1][p]This may not impact you as a player, but the entire stats system is now being calculated differently under the hood, which allows me as a developer to do more fancy stuff with it (which I didn't). [/p][p]The new system allows for per-element, per-weapon-type stat modifications, which wasn't practical with the old system. [/p][p]I'm mostly outlining it here as a fun fact.[/p][p]Anyway, back to non-technical stuff.[/p][p][/p][h1]Effective/Overflow Damage[/h1][p]I've been struggling with balancing out damage numbers for the sake of leaderboards, and I've noticed that the most effective difficulty to play when considering leaderboards is the classic Normal difficulty.[/p][p]The reason being that enemies were easy to kill and farm damage against. [/p][p]So by nature of this system, the players capable of beating the harder difficulties were actively punished for playing them.[/p][p]Starting with 1.9, damage will be split into Effective Damage and Overflow Damage (this is what the toggle in the result screen is for). Effective Damage is the damage used for leaderboard scores; it caps out at a mob's max health, so if the weapon deals 100 damage but the mob has only 5 HP, the leaderboard will add only 5 to the resulting score instead of the original 100.[/p][p]Higher difficulties give enemies more health, which in turn will allow for higher scores, rewarding the commitment to completing those.[/p][p]As a result, leaderboard submissions will again accept scores lower than a million for easier submissions! That means old scores will be easier to beat, but there is no need to wipe them away this time.[/p][p]By default, floating damage numbers will display Effective Damage; you can toggle this in the settings.[/p][p][/p][h1]Post-Processing Settings[/h1][p]You can now disable and enable specific post-processing effects from the settings screen.[/p][p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45228567/52f7a5e124a45fe2e411a2e9f111ee817420560f.jpg"][/img][/p][h1]Damage Numbers[/h1][p]There are some minor changes to the looks of damage numbers.[/p][p][/p][h2]Gradient [/h2][p]Damage numbers got a little bit of a gradient going on; you can toggle this in the settings if you want the single-color ones back.[/p][p][/p][h2]Reaction Merge[/h2][p]Elemental Reactions/Inflictions triggered by the attack will now display alongside the damage number instead of being a separate text instance.[/p][p][/p][h1]New Achievements[/h1][p]There are a few new achievements added to the game. Nishi The Duskbringer and Chitose got their character-specific achievements; more character-specific achievements will come in future versions![/p][p][/p][h1]Perk Tree[/h1][p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45228567/815aa52b8219a76835b33bba856a9f66014bdd77.jpg"][/img][/p][p]I'm not going to stall the release any further. Can't say I'm too happy with it, and things will probably change in the future, but it is functional enough in the current state.[/p][p]You obtain one skill point every time a character levels up (the character level, not the in-game levels!). And those can be used to unlock different nodes that provide a variety of specific buffs.[/p][p]Characters get more difficult to level up over time, so it should nudge you to play other characters for a change. (●'◡'●)[/p][p][/p][h1]The Beginner's Blessing[/h1][p]Version 1.9 will also introduce an additional effect to the [b]Normal[/b] difficulty. [/p][p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45228567/a765c030c034b1c7c9a3fb061bb106a0c8f58969.jpg"][/img][/p][p]I figured unlocking new weapons can be difficult or not obvious for some players, and to make the early experience a bit more interesting when playing the Normal difficulty, players will randomly unlock 3 locked weapons for that run![/p][p]Weapons unlocked this way have a special indicator on the level-up screen.[/p][p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45228567/521ec42dfb31c8be99eb92774940ad05a03b1e10.jpg"][/img][/p][p][/p][h1]New Main Menu Theme[/h1][p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45228567/9804fe6525a3b8ebf4ab882cc70c91d67e133a83.jpg"][/img][/p][p]As for every major version of the game. The main menu theme has also been updated. Reminded that you can always switch back to the old ones from the settings![/p][p][/p][h1]New Steam Assets[/h1][p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45228567/77b0e78c2a6d16bc2014ebaece9f0af7291cce64.png"][/img][/p][p]As you may have noticed I also updated the Steam banner and game header to match the current aesthetics! It's old, but new![/p][p][/p][h1]Minor Improvements and Bug Fixes[/h1][list][*][p][b]Memory Rifts [/b]will now reward additional gold and gems upon entering them.[/p][/*][*][p]Previously selected stage will now be remembered [/p][/*][*][p]Added option to quickly reset filters in Collection and Achievement menus[/p][/*][*][p]Added back the STPP upscaling method to the settings (should work correctly now)[/p][/*][*][p]Added dot shadow at enemies' feet[/p][/*][*][p]Renamed game speed settings to closer reflect their meaning[/p][/*][*][p]Removed unreleased maps from various menu filters[/p][/*][*][p]Removed AI narrator when selecting characters (it was annoying)[/p][/*][*][p]Fixed scrolling in settings that only worked when hovering over a setting entry[/p][/*][*][p]Discarding relics via the recollection popup will now correctly grant relic pieces[/p][/*][*][p]Added pop-up notification when trying to perform Recollection without sufficient amount of gems[/p][/*][*][p]Fixed [i]Amelia's[/i] title that didn't match the achievement text[/p][/*][*][p]Fixed elemental reaction events not triggering when damage numbers were disabled[/p][/*][*][p]Fixed a bug that prevented players from closing the character list with the Escape button[/p][/*][*][p]Fixed a potential bug that could cause screen controls to show up on PCs with no touch support[/p][/*][*][p]Fixed UI text blur caused by anti-aliasing[/p][/*][*][p]Fixed incorrect orientation of the [b]Lightning Spear[/b] projectiles[/p][/*][*][p]Fixed an error occurring when exiting the run[/p][/*][/list][p][/p][h1]Afterword[/h1][p]I spent a long time working on this update—4 months if I'm not mistaken—and I still failed to deliver everything I intended to. For that, I'm very sorry (┬┬﹏┬┬)[/p][p][/p][p]Unfortunately, it turns out writing is not my strong suit. As much as I had the bigger picture of the story in mind, I failed to fully patch up and tie together all the smaller plot points—which, in the end, turned out to not be so minor after all.[/p][p]The story will come out before or with 2.0. That much, you have my word![/p][p]Another thing I fell short on (though I at least provided a partial implementation) is the perk tree. I went through a bunch of iterations but ultimately couldn’t find anything I felt was good enough. I even went as far as rewriting the entire stat system (which took weeks of development time) to make the perk tree more flexible, but it still didn’t do as much as I’d hoped. [/p][p]I’ll continue iterating on that system in future versions. Worst case scenario, we’ll stick with what we have, and I’ll just expand it by adding more nodes.[/p][p][/p][p]But enough about the failures![/p][p]I shaped 1.9 up to be the biggest update to Requiem For a Lost World to date. Whether I succeeded or not is up for you to decide, but personally I’m happy with it (even if I expected to cram in even more content).[/p][p]Working on it without a tight deadline was also pretty nice. I’ll admit I took breaks in between features, but I didn’t end up beating myself up over it, which was refreshing.[/p][p]The new character assets look pretty good as well. There’s still some room for improvement since I cut corners on the backgrounds, but nothing that can’t be fixed later.[/p][p]Speaking of the future—the next version shouldn’t be too far off, though I’d like to aim for 2.0 right away. [/p][p]Here’s an overview of what I expect to be working on (not a definitive list):[/p][list][*][p]A new map: Forbidden Zone  [/p][/*][*][p]A new character: Clara  [/p][/*][*][p]Shop UI improvements  [/p][/*][*][p]Possibly a main menu improvement  [/p][/*][*][p]CO-OP improvements  [/p][/*][/list][p]I especially want to focus on stabilizing the CO-OP experience since it’s pretty bumpy right now—and probably only got worse in this version.[/p][p]In preparation for the full release in 2.0, I’ll also be focusing on smaller additions like more achievements, name cards, and skins. These will take priority over some of the elements listed above.[/p][p]Of course, 2.0 is still some months off, so we’ll see what makes it into the release version.[/p][p]For now, thank you all for the support, and I’ll see you around for the next patch notes![/p][p][/p]

notes.title: The Road Out of Early Access: Feedback Wanted
notes.content:
[h1]Hello everyone![/h1]

The last update came out a while ago, and the next one likely won’t be dropping anytime soon either. So I wanted to take a moment to share some thoughts, gather your feedback, and shape the future version of the game together.

Since Steam isn’t the best platform for collecting feedback—and the in-game survey isn’t well-suited for early development ideas—I’ve decided to make a separate post to show you what I’m working on for version [b]1.9[/b], hear your thoughts, and get your input!

[h2]Early Access Extension[/h2]

As many of you probably know, [i]Requiem For a Lost World[/i] was originally scheduled to release in Q2 2025. Clearly, that’s not going to happen. I’ll be extending the Early Access period by another six months.

That said, I’d like to hear your thoughts:  
[list]
[*] What would make [i]Requiem[/i] feel ready for a full release in your eyes?  
[*] Are there unresolved issues that need fixing first?  
[*] Is the content lacking, or are there specific features [i]you[/i] want to see in the final version?
[/list]

Ideally, I’d like to release version [b]1.9[/b] in the coming months (with a few follow-up patches), and then aim for [b]2.0[/b] as the final major release around November.

Since 1.9 may include some pretty big changes I’m still unsure about, I’d love to get your input before locking things in.

[h2]Shard Asset Changes[/h2]

Let’s talk about art. I know AI-generated assets are a dealbreaker for some of you, especially when they carry that telltale “AI look.” That’s why I’ve decided to redo all the shard assets from scratch with a different style—honestly, they needed some love anyway.

Here’s a quick before-and-after comparison (left = old, right = new):  
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45228567/aa02a52d44851787677388478732ddee6ac532ce.jpg[/img]

I chose examples that aren’t too far off from the originals. Don’t mind the artifacts on the new ones—they haven’t been touched up yet.

Do you think these are an improvement? Some are now more reflective of the character’s story, instead of just being random visuals.

I also experimented with updating the [b]character cards[/b], but the results didn’t turn out as well. The new cards don’t quite fit into the current UI. Still, here’s a preview:  
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45228567/ae907f26dea2462891438553f405c54072bf51d3.jpg[/img]

Changing the cards might eventually require updating the pixel graphics too, so let me know if you think it's worth it!

[h2]Story Changes[/h2]

In the same artistic spirit, I’ll also be rewriting the story text on each shard. I’m pretty happy with the writing direction for the latest characters, so I’ll be following that style going forward.

Each shard should tell a piece of a character’s story—and hopefully, once you’ve collected all of them, you’ll be able to piece together a fuller narrative. Some characters might even need more than five shards to do their story justice.

The [i]Story[/i] tab is temporarily removed from the main menu, but it will return once I settle on how it should be presented. If you have suggestions, I’d love to hear them!

I’m also thinking about introducing [b]chapter-based story segments[/b] that focus less on the overall plot (since that will be told through shards) and more on key events that don’t fit well into the shard format.

[h2]Character Reworks[/h2]

There’s a pretty noticeable gap in kit complexity between old and new characters. Older ones often don’t use newer systems and sometimes lack a strong identity.

For version 1.9, I’m planning to adjust—or completely rework—most characters up to [b]Amelisana[/b].

If there’s anyone in particular you’d like to see reworked, let me know!

[h2]Perk Tree and Meta Systems[/h2]

The character reworks will improve the meta by themselves, but I’ve also been exploring ways to expand progression—and that’s led me to the idea of [b]skill trees[/b].

Unfortunately, implementing something interesting will mean rewriting a core part of the game again: the stat and damage system.

Here’s an early peek at what the skill tree might look like (subject to change):  
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45228567/223818738bdb90f4d2dfaa6003c0ba1b48c6f8cb.jpg[/img]

What would you like to see in this system? What would you [i]not[/i] want?

[h2]Relic Sub-Stats[/h2]

Another potential addition is [b]relic sub-stats[/b]—not as extreme as in typical gacha games, but still something that adds depth.

Here’s a preview:  
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45228567/c0fbaaadee076959b86f17f7e017c718325b01b4.jpg[/img]

It’s a change I [i]could[/i] make—but [b]should[/b] I? I know some of you already find relics a bit overwhelming.

If implemented, there would be ways to reroll and upgrade sub-stats through gameplay and minigames.

[h2]Roadmap Summary[/h2]

Here’s what version 1.9 is shaping up to include, depending on your feedback:

[list]
[*] [b]New/improved shard art[/b]  
 [i]→ Do you like them? Prefer the old ones?[/i]

[*] [b]Shard story rewrites[/b]  
 [i]→ What do you think of piecing the story together this way?[/i]

[*] [b]Character reworks[/b]  
 [i]→ Adam and Chitose are first in line. Any others you want to see reworked?[/i]

[*] [b]Relic sub-stats[/b]  
 [i]→ Are you in favor or against this system?[/i]
[/list]

[h2]Looking Ahead[/h2]

You’re always welcome to share your ideas—whether it’s for version 1.9, 2.0, or even beyond. If something is small enough, I might be able to squeeze it into 1.9. Bigger ideas can help shape the future of the game.

[b]Even if you’ve never commented before,[/b] please don’t hesitate to speak up!  
I read every message, and your feedback—no matter how small—can help guide the game in the right direction. Whether it's a concern, a wish, or just something you like, it really helps more than you might think.

Between 1.9 and 2.0, the focus will mostly be on polishing, bug fixes, and [b]co-op improvements[/b].

Version [b]2.0[/b] will also bring a new map: the [i]Forbidden Zone[/i], complete with new enemies, weapons, and a new character.

As for [i]The Abyss[/i], I haven’t had time to work on it yet, so it may not make it into the full release—but it’s still something I want to return to in the future.

And just so there’s no confusion:  
[b][u]2.0 is just the end of Early Access, not the end of support![/u][/b]  
More content updates will continue even after the full release.

Thanks again for playing—and if you’ve got thoughts, now’s a great time to share them!

notes.title: Version Update 1.8.4
notes.content:
Hello everyone!

It’s me again—the dev—bringing you another update!  
This one’s a bit lighter on content since I’ve been focusing hard on performance for both high- and low-end devices. But we’ll get into that in just a moment (●'◡'●)

First things first: as mentioned in the last patch notes, [b]Leaderboards have been reset![/b]  
Good luck, and happy hunting!

Now let’s dive into the juicy stuff!

[h1]Nyxaria Joins the Battle[/h1]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45228567/96fb652f2851632bbeeedb8f78a36529224e9506.png[/img]

Nyxaria—formerly known simply as Aria—a [b]Cosmic DoT DPS[/b] specialist! She’s a powerhouse when it comes to building up elemental effects, and her passive dramatically increases DoT tick rate (with a trade-off in duration).

Her signature weapon, the [b]Judgement of Nyx[/b], cuts through not only enemies but the very fabric of space itself, applying [i]Cosmic DoT[/i] in a wide arc.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45228567/8f254a661deb39ddb5dbd5dce3d4bdace47f9b1e.gif[/img]

Her ultimate, [b]Collapse of Aeons[/b], is a 3-stage channeling ability triggered by [i]holding down[/i] the skill button.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45228567/b07af8ca426bc9f0659277998514344d486b44c7.gif[/img]

(GIF is sped up due to file size limits)

As you hold the button, Nyxaria rains cosmic fire from above, increasing in intensity the longer it’s held—dealing more damage, but consuming more of her health per second.

[h1]Elemental Accumulation[/h1]

Elemental Accumulation is a new mechanic designed to reward single-element and rapid-hit builds.

Repeatedly applying the same element to enemies triggers unique effects. These scale with elemental effect buffs and fade over time, so fast attacks are key!

Here’s a breakdown of the new accumulation effects:

[list]
[*] [b]Ignition[/b] – [i]Fire[/i]: Deals 5% of the target’s max HP every 0.5s for 5s.
[*] [b]Overload[/b] – [i]Lightning[/i]: Stuns for 0.3s and deals 2% max HP every 0.5s for 5s.
[*] [b]Frostbite[/b] – [i]Ice[/i]: Slows by 40% for 3s and deals a burst of damage equal to the triggering hit.
[*] [b]Wounded[/b] – [i]Physical[/i]: Bleeds for 40% of the hit damage every 0.5s for 5s.
[*] [b]Burst[/b] – [i]Wind[/i]: Your next attack after this deals 150% damage.
[*] [b]Radiance[/b] – [i]Light[/i]: Reduces a random elemental defense by 20% (stacks).
[*] [b]Singularity[/b] – [i]Cosmic[/i]: Makes reactions and accumulations 15% stronger vs. the target (stacks).
[*] [b]Shadowbind[/b] – [i]Dark[/i]: After 4s, deals damage equal to current HP. Reapplying shortens the delay by 0.3s.
[*] [b]Petrify[/b] – [i]Earth[/i]: Stuns for 0.5s and reduces physical defense by 20%.
[/list]

I hope you enjoy messing around with builds and discovering combos!

[h1]Damage Indicators[/h1]

You’ll now see red screen edges flash when taking 5+ damage. A similar effect appears when reviving—check out the Nyxaria ult GIF above!

You can toggle this in the settings menu.

Also, player damage numbers are now an optional display—when taking or healing at least 1 HP, you'll see numbers above your character. Toggle that in the settings too!

[h1]New Damage Numbers[/h1]

Out with the old, in with the shiny new:

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45228567/320a4e94d04674e8c7f50d03503b987dd5ce218a.jpg[/img]

You can customize how they behave! Let them explode all over your screen or vanish quickly—it’s up to you. More visual effects may come in the future!

[h1]New Difficulty System[/h1]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45228567/61efab9b0131d4362ce31834ef29de7605d89269.jpg[/img]

Difficulties are now split into more gradual stages:

[olist]
[*] Normal
[*] Shallow I–V
[*] Deep I–V
[/olist]

Deep levels come with special enemy effects for added challenge.  
Details are visible on the difficulty list to the right of the selection screen.

[h1]Leaderboards[/h1]

As mention before leaderboards have been reset!
Time to rise through the ranks all over again—good luck out there!

But that’s not all—there are some changes to how scoring works!  
Previously, scores were calculated based only on [b]weapon damage[/b], which meant elemental reactions and ultimates didn’t count. That felt a bit unfair.

Starting from [b]v1.8.4[/b], your [b]total damage dealt[/b] is now what matters—this includes everything: weapons, elemental reactions and ultimates.

You can even see it on the result screen:

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45228567/075122c7e11a476669764781281decaa584239e1.jpg[/img]

Oh, and here’s the real kicker...

You can now [b]view the builds[/b] players used for their leaderboard runs!  
Ever wonder how someone pulled off that crazy high score? Wonder no more:

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45228567/3b0c57aa4aa64644e976ba8bf66c5a4740b1496c.jpg[/img]

You can even copy their build directly to try it out for yourself.

[h1]Quality of Life Improvements[/h1]

[h2]Camera Zoom[/h2]  
Scroll in or out with your mouse wheel. Finally!

[h2]Shop Sliders[/h2]  
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45228567/a9aa5cd2227ca641eaf538f2106f5bc159c3935e.jpg[/img]  
Buy items in bulk (except for upgrades). Save those clicks!

[h2]Fragment Overlay Cleanup[/h2]  
Removed extra lines that obscured shard graphics.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45228567/8e7466c6c44dee2a9dbd27e69e21186c27fd34fd.jpg[/img]

[h2]Memory Fragments[/h2]  
Memory Fragments (EXP shards) will no longer be merged when within camera view.

[h1]Performance Optimizations[/h1]

[h2]Nature Renderer[/h2]  
New experimental GPU Instancing toggle in settings (off by default).  
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45228567/e35a23a5cb5cbf9210b2fe650ab3327b9e0ddb35.jpg[/img]

Implemented only on the Capital Outskirts map (the only grassy one). Yields better performance at high distances/densities. May not work well on older hardware.

[h2]Code Optimizations[/h2]  
Refactored code for pickups, damage numbers, enemy logic, and projectiles.  
Result: Better FPS across the board—up to double in crowded scenes.

[h2]Pickup Animation Toggle[/h2]  
Disable pickup animations to save CPU power. It’s subtle but helpful!

[h2]Performance Tips[/h2]

If your FPS still drops:

[list]
[*] Disable damage numbers in late game
[*] Minimap can cause FPS dips
[*] Turn off antialiasing and ambient occlusion (huge help on integrated GPUs)
[/list]

Friendly reminder that I provide the max settings that are completely overkill most of the time. If your PC sounds like it's about to take off it may be a good idea to reduce grass/tree render distance and density

[h1]Bug Fixes[/h1]

[h2]Sprite Rendering[/h2]  
Animated sprites were misbehaving—appearing in front of things they shouldn’t. That’s all been fixed!

[h2]DoT Scaling[/h2]  
DoTs now scale properly with elemental damage, resistance penetration, and reaction bonuses!

[h2]Misc Fixes[/h2]

[list]
[*] Yami-no-Tokyia’s animated sprite was missing—she’s back!
[*] Madra’s sprite was misaligned—now fixed.
[*] Game result screen was skipping if switching between skinned/non-skinned characters.
[*] Crate icon no longer spins with you on the minimap.
[*] Character tuning icon was incorrectly labeled as “Relics.”
[*] Tuning icon now properly greys out for locked characters.
[*] Kaware’s shop fragment title fixed from "echo of peace" to "fragment of peace."
[/list]

[h1]Afterword[/h1]

That’s it for this patch!  
Lots of work for a "small" update ┌(。Д。)┐ but more is on the way!

[h2]Recollection Animations (WIP)[/h2]

No promises, but I want to try adding these as unique pull animations.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45228567/f056440378df23541257359d02b9be9737df1bff.gif[/img]

Here's an early mockup for Nyxaria—not in-game yet, but I hope to give every character something like this!

[h2]A New Progression System?[/h2]

With the expanded difficulty system, I’m exploring a new layer of progression.  
We’ve got shop upgrades, relics, and item unlocks already... so what’s next?

The idea: use [b]character levels[/b] to power up a new system—something like a big PoE-style passive tree.  
Level up characters, unlock paths, and tailor builds even further!  
That’s the dream (≧∇≦)ﾉ

[h2]Further Optimizations[/h2]
I’ll continue keeping an eye on bottlenecks and frame-hogging systems, and aim to bring even more optimizations in future updates.  

[h2]Gameplay Tutorials[/h2]
I’m working on expanding tutorial pop-ups directly into the gameplay area to make things clearer and more intuitive as you play.  
No more guessing what buttons do or what the weird rocks are for

[hr]

Thanks for reading! As always I will be waiting for any suggestions and opinions regarding new features!

notes.title: Version Update 1.8.3
notes.content: Hello everyone! The new update is back on schedule, and today's changes mostly focus on implementing features requested on Discord! (｡･∀･)ﾉﾞ It's a smaller update, but I hope you'll enjoy the new additions! For now, I'll address one particular point from a review: [h1]Character Animations[/h1] [img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45228567/ce39556ddb9f75261ba259d2104d670309858525.gif[/img] This update introduces idle animations for every playable character. Each one has its own rig, unlike the frame animations used for enemies. This makes animations much smoother and easier to adjust in the future if needed. I also updated several heavily outdated character sprites and cleaned up some AI artifacts in the rest—at least to the best of my ability. Characters with updated sprites: [list] [*] Eliza [*] Oana [*] Nishi (Vanquisher of Faith) [*] Arika [*] Chitose [*] Summer [*] Amelia (Bearer of Dream) [*] Natalie [*] Truzi [/list] As for animations like walking or perspective shifts, maintaining consistency with AI tools remains challenging. Further improvements may be possible as tools evolve. [h1]Menu Extensions[/h1] [h2]Pause Menu[/h2] [img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45228567/5de6f071a8513b71f4899b774fdc5a2c07cb82fe.jpg[/img] The pause menu now features two additional options: [list] [*] Collection [*] Tutorials [/list] If you need a refresher on mechanics or want to browse available items to plan future level-ups, these options should help! Additionally, I've expanded the stat list display. You can toggle between these options in the settings: [list] [*] Simple - The same as before, displaying only essential stats [*] Full list - Shows most character stats available in the game [*] Non-zero - Displays only modified stats (affected by items, relics, or character abilities) [/list] These settings also apply to the character selection screen! And one more pause menu fix: pressing Escape will no longer close the entire pause screen when exiting submenus. [h2]Character Selection[/h2] [img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45228567/ca05bef5913a8cdb1de467af5928ece99ee1e844.jpg[/img] Tired of clicking through every character to find ones with half-full or empty relic pages? Character cards now display the number of occupied slots on their relic pages. [h2]Collection Screen[/h2] You can now quickly ban items by right-clicking their collection entry—no more jumping between screens! [h2]Relic Rewards Pop-up[/h2] You can now close the pop-up by clicking anywhere—no need to aim for the confirm button anymore! [h2]Relic Discard Notification[/h2] [img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45228567/5339389fde20a2adee7829874ea33f4e5b35c3c2.jpg[/img] Mass-discarding relics? The game will now notify you of how many relics will be discarded based on the selected filter. Also, I fixed an issue where the rarity filter didn’t work properly when multiple options were selected. [h2]Steam Profile Banners[/h2] I'm growing more unhappy with the main menu by the day （︶^︶） As part of a potential future rework, I decided to improve a long-neglected feature: [img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45228567/41d8c067e1b4a7e1a5a28f7d023372ab1bbadfa7.jpg[/img] The top-left corner now displays your Steam avatar and nickname as before, but also your global ranking—an average of your leaderboard rankings across all maps. You can also change the banner graphic by clicking the small settings button: [img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45228567/6f60489ca69dcec7f8be9c070013c30128197628.jpg[/img] Banners unlock via achievements, with more coming from events and the shop! [h2]More Minimap Settings[/h2] [img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45228567/bbe50efb81ad4c6be4ba99b70ff04eeab34e07ad.jpg[/img] More minimap marker toggles have been added to help declutter the map! You can also choose whether the map rotates with the character or stays fixed while icons rotate. [h1]Shop Changes[/h1] [h2]Amelisana Fragments[/h2] Amelisana's fragments have been added to the shop! [h2]Item Seals[/h2] The number of weapon/item bans is now limited. However, you can purchase Item Seals (up to 20) from the shop to increase this limit. [img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45228567/8c596e62ab7df2abc364a3e59f830b93d1354e5f.jpg[/img] As a result, existing item bans will be reset. Sorry for the inconvenience ~(>_<。) But on the bright side—banning items no longer disqualifies you from the leaderboards! [h1]Character Tuning[/h1] Did you really think I'd take away item bans without an alternative? This feature is still in testing, and I'll tweak it based on feedback! Character Tuning lets you set up a build plan for each character, accessible from the character card: [img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45228567/33e8a9a38b3d7a1e044051b99b4d734dacd5c0e1.jpg[/img] Each character has their own build plan: [img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45228567/9922ac70fbbbfbb06f574e9c8aeaa1ba1ea68ad1.jpg[/img] You can specify up to 6 weapons and 6 items per character. Items in the build will have a higher chance of appearing (even if banned in the collection). Build items are marked during level-ups: [img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45228567/7c23bef48cdd3e6a8b457830f34d4a7a7118ad02.jpg[/img] Right-clicking an item in the list will open a quick summary pop-up: [img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45228567/34e2284ea12884ba2a0d76eed15952c22b3398dd.jpg[/img] [h1]Rebalancing[/h1] [h2]Difficulty Adjustments[/h2] Difficulties beyond [i]Normal[/i] have been buffed—perhaps too much—but given what I've seen on the leaderboards, I think you'll manage. [h2]Enemy Relics[/h2] Relics affecting enemy health, spawn rates, and counts now increase these stats instead of reducing them, allowing you to push higher leaderboard scores! [h1]Leaderboards[/h1] Some of you are way too powerful. The highest score is currently 1.7kkk, dangerously close to Steam's 2.1kkk limit. To prevent overflow, scores will be stored in a reduced format starting at 100k. Since I can't edit existing scores, the leaderboards will be wiped next patch ┗( T﹏T )┛ Compensation will be issued prior to that. [h1]Cloud Save[/h1] Cloud saving is finally enabled! Your saves should now sync across devices. [h1]Minor Changes and Fixes[/h1] [list] [*] Fixed typo in the Infernal Gate series of upgrades for Portal weapon [*] Fixed missing description of Darkened Resolve (II) [*] Fixed the Recollection pull button accepting clicks even after animation have already started [*] Fixed Corina's ultimate cooldown being abnormally short [*] Fixed key rebinding during gameplay being retriggered by a space button [*] Fixed the recollection menu animation missing animation for the tutorial button [*] Dreya's Withering state will no longer grant her additional damage based on character level [*] Fixed Kaware's summons fail to spawn in CO-OP scenario [/list] [h1]Afterword[/h1] Hey, the dev here (≧∇≦)ﾉ Previous plans are still ongoing. I'm also rewriting the story fragments on characters and will probably update them in a small update soonish when I'm done! I mean, just the wording since the story is pretty much done at this point, I just have to tell it ┌(。Д。)┐ I've been thinking about pushing the early access period further since the Q2 seems less realistic now. I will of course continue updating the game even past the EA period, but I want to have a proper release be fun and bug free with a lot more features, to hopefully not flop! Once again, big thanks for suggestions and see you next update!

notes.title: Version Update 1.8.2
notes.content:
Hey!  

It's been a little while since the last update. I'll go into more details at the end of this post, but for now, let's dive into the changes! (≧∇≦)ﾉ  

[h1]New Characters[/h1]  

Once again, I'm bringing you a batch of three new characters in a single update!  

[h2]Ondines[/h2]  

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45228567/8980c8e5e09dcff4d1a095dccb613e78f82eb38f.jpg[/img]  

Ondines is a physical tank-type character, meaning he can take a beating [i]and[/i] hit back just as hard—a desirable trait for a Royal Guard and a member of the 2nd Delver's Platoon.  

His weapon of choice is a trusty war hammer, perfect for crushing enemies with sheer force.  

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45228567/539e56eae07e7a502cebf15246ec6178d6482da0.gif[/img]  

If smashing things with a hammer isn't enough, his ultimate, [b]Unstoppable[/b], allows him to swing his weapon freely while gaining a 100% armor boost.  

However, wearing such heavy armor comes at a cost of mobility. Ondines can generate a shield to block direct damage, but the heavier the shield, the slower he moves.  

In CO-OP, he’s also more likely to be targeted by enemies, taking the pressure off his teammates.  

[hr][/hr]  
[i]Dev Notes[/i]  
I received a few requests for characters that work better in CO-OP, so I wanted to lean into that. I hope having a tank-style character will be fun to play in both single-player and multiplayer.  

Ondines is also the first armor-scaling character, which was quite a challenge to balance. But I think the movement tradeoff adds an interesting dynamic. Needless to say, he probably [i]won’t[/i] be the best pick for exploration. (｡･∀･)ﾉﾞ  

[h2]Kaware[/h2]  

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45228567/8f819c54878d8f11536401f04e6e11cd6c0fb645.jpg[/img]  

Kaware is a summon-type character.  
But wait, what exactly is a [b]summon type[/b]?  

The last update introduced the new [b]Dark[/b] element with its own mechanics. [b]Summons[/b], on the other hand, are a new type of weapon (right now, there’s only one summon weapon, but more are planned for the future). These weapons don’t fire projectiles but instead summon creatures to fight by your side!  

Summons spawn with set damage and health, cannot be hit by enemies, but their health drains over time—the longer they exist, the faster they decay.  

Now that we've cleared that up, let's introduce Kaware and her pet wolves!  

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45228567/96723c5d9f77a5366922de5e18e9ba5376402efd.gif[/img]  

These wolves automatically seek out nearby enemies, dealing [b]Lightning[/b] damage on contact.  

But that’s not all Kaware can do. She also doubles as a healer—for both characters and summons. Her ultimate, [b]Magical Forest[/b], creates an enchanted forest that damages enemies while healing all allies within its boundaries.  

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45228567/0174d0b8c202245d87248cc7523138464ce6bca8.gif[/img]  

As the Sanctuary’s top scout, Kaware has spent countless hours beyond the city walls, patrolling dense forests for threats. Whenever she found an injured animal, she always tried to nurse it back to health. Naturally, that ability extended to healing humans too—though her methods can be a bit crude.  

[hr][/hr]  
[i]Dev Notes[/i]  
I’ve wanted to make a summon-based character for a while. Lucy laid some groundwork for it long ago, and I finally got around to implementing it. Hopefully, you’ll have fun experimenting with summons!  

Kaware herself is still in an early state—her role leans heavily into summon DPS/support, but there aren’t many summons in the game yet. In the meantime, she pairs well with Earth weapons!  

Also, while we have plenty of characters that thrive on low HP, Kaware is the opposite—she performs best when she stays healthy~  

[h2]Dreya[/h2]  

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45228567/582591d7240e496ce94b35b2e85b26faab53dc23.jpg[/img]  

Dreya is a Dark-element, Follow-Up DPS. A serious and dangerous explorer of the Forbidden Zones, she is the sole member of Diver Squad 6. Her job? To venture deep beyond the Sanctuary’s borders, recovering rare and potentially valuable relics for the Capital.  

Her weapon of choice? Anything will do! But she always carries a hidden Dark Blade that feeds on her life force. Whenever Dreya takes damage, she immediately counterattacks with her blade, dealing Dark damage in a follow-up strike.  

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45228567/383720f7e34e4638d946839fcb3da359fb4aa6d1.gif[/img]  

Her ultimate applies [b]Withering[/b] to herself, draining a percentage of her health over time—fueling her deadly blade in the process.  

On the rare occasion that she has to work with others, Dreya's follow-up attacks restore [b]Special[/b] energy for both herself and her teammates.  

[hr][/hr]  
[i]Dev Notes[/i]  
It was about time Follow-Ups got their own dedicated character. Yami-no-Tokiya had some follow-up mechanics, but I wanted a character that truly embraced the playstyle. After many iterations, I think I’ve landed on a design that is unique in its own way while allowing follow-up attacks to shine.  

Continuing the trend of CO-OP-oriented synergy, Dreya’s ability to restore [b]Special[/b] should come in handy with some characters!  

[h1]Minimap[/h1]  

As you may have noticed in previous screenshots, [i]Requiem For a Lost Worldi[/i] is finally getting a minimap! It can be enabled in the settings and offers some customization options.  

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45228567/cf0183bf3f3db621cfa6dd3ae6f6ccdc9d9742e5.jpg[/img]  

The minimap displays active shrines in CO-OP, unexplored locations, pickups, and more. If you prefer to find things on your own, you can disable the location pointers.  

It does come with a slight performance hit, but hopefully, nothing too crazy.  

[h1]Leaderboards[/h1]  

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45228567/2feee4263c88dc0e1f76e4bdbe2e84d08d7023fc.jpg[/img]  

I've seen a few requests for matchmaking in the past, but I don't think we have nearly enough players for that to work ┌(。Д。)┐  

So instead, I’ve implemented leaderboards! Players can choose to participate—or completely ignore them. This should add some interaction between players outside of CO-OP without relying on a large player base.  

[i]Requiem For a Lost World[/i] is... well, mostly unbalanced, so I wouldn’t take the leaderboards *too* seriously. Or would I? (. ❛ ᴗ ❛.)  

Leaderboards will likely reset from time to time when major balance patches roll out.  

Oh, and [b]endless mode doesn’t count[/b] toward leaderboards!  

[h1]Relic Fragments[/h1]  

Another patch, another relic-related update. It’s a tradition at this point—  

Anyway, discarding relics will now have a purpose beyond just freeing up space. Whenever you discard a relic, you’ll receive [b]Relic Fragments[/b], with higher-rarity relics yielding more fragments. These can then be used in the [b]Synthesizer[/b] to increase the roll value of crafted relics.  

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45228567/cb0c3261ffe3448735e4a66dba7ba6c8c4fd46a4.jpg[/img]  

You can increase a relic’s roll value up to three times, with each upgrade costing 100 fragments.  

[h1]Relic Shop[/h1]  

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45228567/21ac7c378ba1823998cd137d81f683812b7c799d.jpg[/img]  

You can now buy relics directly from the shop! Five relics will cost around 1000 gems—slightly more efficient than pulling from Recollection.  

[h1]Tutorial Menu Rework[/h1]  

Tutorials have always been one of [i]Requiem For a Lost World[/i]'s weak points. Nobody likes writing documentation, and the gameplay loop of survivor-likes seems simple enough, right? Wrong!  

The core gameplay is still very much a survivor-like, but everything around it has become much more complex over time. The last patch introduced menu tutorials to help new players navigate the UI and understand basic features.  

This update expands the in-game "wiki," which has been a bit neglected until now.  

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45228567/e5d731157c8d3dd5b03994cc3bb2a65e9d6b042f.jpg[/img]  

I'll be gradually adding more content to make it a proper knowledge base for the game. Whether you're a new player or a veteran, I encourage you to check it out—and feedback is always appreciated!  

[h1]Balance Changes[/h1]  

I've adjusted the [b]difficulty curve[/b] for the first and second stages. Previously, difficulty increased on a full-minute basis. Now, the curve is smoother, so difficulty ramps up more gradually even within the same wave of enemies. The game should feel slightly more challenging as a result.  

[b]Capital Undergrounds[/b] now has [i]fewer[/i] enemies overall, but each one is tougher (more HP and damage—because that’s what difficulty means, right?). The overall challenge should remain similar, but single-target damage will be more effective.  

[b]Elemental Reactions[/b] have received a significant buff. You should now see them dealing much more damage against tankier enemies (you can’t even set up reactions on weak enemies, after all). The goal of this change is to make elemental reactions a bigger part of the game by making enemies tankier—so using reactions will help bring them down much faster.  

[b]Follow-Up[/b] type weapons have also received a hefty buff to their base damage, allowing them to scale better with % damage increases from their dedicated upgrades.  

[h1]Enemies Removed from Collection[/h1]  

I've temporarily removed enemies from the collection menu. I hated how it looked.  

It’ll be readded once I figure out a better way to display them.  

[h1]Writing Changes[/h1]  

Kaware, Dreya, and Ondines have a different writing style for their stories. I’d love to hear feedback from those of you who care about the lore!  

If the response is positive, I’ll gradually rewrite the stories of other characters to match this new style. Let me know what you think!  

[h1]Save File Changes[/h1]  

To reduce leaderboard cheating, save files are now encrypted. This means older versions of the game will no longer be able to read them.  

The game will automatically create a backup in the game folder, just in case something goes wrong.  

If your save file gets corrupted, please report it in the Steam discussions, and we’ll try to find a solution.  

We haven’t encountered any issues in testing, but better safe than sorry!  

[h1]Login Event[/h1]  

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45228567/74c598dfc018e099d0c439fb073cfadafe7ec439.jpg[/img]  

Log in for 7 days before the end of March to claim a free Ondines and a bunch of high-quality relics!  

[h1]Bug Fixes[/h1]

[list]
[*] Fixed scrolling in the settings UI bugging out and not working properly
[*] Moved spawn location in the Capital Undergrounds to prevent taking damage while spawning
[*] Fixed passive text not fitting text bubble correctly on some characters
[*] Fixed damage accumulation and hitbox of [b]Gift Box[/b] weapon
[/list]

[h1]Afterword[/h1]

If you were here for the changelog, you're free to go! Or wait, leave a comment first! If you’d like to read some rambling from the developer, feel free to continue.  

I would like to encourage everyone to leave a positive review if you haven't yet (｡･∀･)ﾉﾞ

[h3]Development Time[/h3]

I’ve taken a few breaks while developing this update, and honestly, they were necessary. I felt the quality of my recent patches had been slipping, mostly because I was setting arbitrary deadlines for myself—and I hated it.  

Getting content out quickly is still important to me, but quality has to come first. I have a history of taking both long and short breaks before releasing on Steam, so this isn’t the first time, and it won’t be the last. Rest assured, content will continue to come out—just at my own pace. Some days, I feel like working on *Requiem For a Lost World* nonstop. Other days, I don’t even want to look at the project files.  

Working on Ondines, Kaware, and Dreya took a long time, but I’m happy with how they turned out. I don’t want to rush summons, so I pushed them back instead of cranking out a bunch of meaningless stat weapons just to meet a quota. Hopefully, that comes across clearly.  

[h3]AI Stuff[/h3]

Another topic I’d like to address is the recent AI witch hunt. My stance on this should be obvious, given that the game uses AI-generated assets.  

People argue over whether AI-generated content is "art" in the traditional sense, but to me, it doesn’t matter what label it gets. I wouldn’t call myself an artist just because I use AI—but I am still a game developer, and making art is, unfortunately, a necessary part of that.  

I haven’t personally been targeted by AI hate, but advertising *Requiem For a Lost World* has been nearly impossible. The entire project gets discredited and written off as "slop" purely because AI was used in some areas of development.  

I wanted to make a free game. I still spend money on it without expecting anything in return. The truth is, I simply can’t afford an artist who can deliver the quality I need within a reasonable timeframe. I also don’t have 10 years to learn how to draw, nor is it a skill I particularly want to learn. AI allowed me to create the game I always wanted to make without compromising too much.  

I code everything, make VFX, debug, and test all features alone. It takes hours every day on top of my 9–5 job. So yeah, it’s really, *really* discouraging to see all of that effort dismissed as "AI-generated slop."  

Because of this, I haven’t been advertising the game at all—I just don’t have the energy to deal with it. At this point, I’m mostly relying on word of mouth.  
[i]Shoutout to the guy on Reddit who randomly recommended this game![/i]  

[h3]Future Features[/h3]

[*] If you played the preview version or saw the news on Discord, you might have noticed I tested something called [i]Visions of Calamity[/i]. It was meant to be a competitive, seasonal game mode feeding into the leaderboards, but I scrapped it from the latest build. Too many bugs, too little time~ It’ll return in a future version.  

[*] Unity recently added a neat little package that helps developers inspect their projects for performance issues.  
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45228567/14d086c7512780569e9511f4496b9cd90e09109d.jpg[/img]  
And wow, game development is *so* different from what I do on a daily basis.  

Anyway, I’ll be going through this list—probably across multiple updates—cleaning up this mess of a project. Hopefully, I can squeeze out some extra FPS here and there!  

[*] Elemental Accumulation is still on the table. I initially avoided it due to network concerns, but I think I can make it work—possibly with a new character designed around this playstyle.

notes.title: Update 1.8.1
notes.content:
[b]Hello, everyone![/b]

It's been a while since the last update, but I’ve been taking things slow as I haven’t been feeling up to the challenge, even with the limited scope. Considering I don’t really have a set update schedule, I think you’re probably used to these random update times by now. (｡･∀･)ﾉﾞ

[h1]New Collection Menu[/h1]

Let’s start off with a new collection menu:

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45228567/a66b00097f8774e274cc8c6d2b1bbf2cd6923163.jpg[/img]

As you can see, it has received a similar treatment to the achievement menu from the previous update. You can filter each section and combine elements or weapon types however you like. But that’s not all!

Clicking on an item now opens a new window with detailed information:

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45228567/16fe6b9549b55f1de06813e81afb86feac44b238.jpg[/img]

This brings us to the new feature: [b]item banning[/b]!

[h2]Item Bans[/h2]

With the growing number of weapons and items available in the game, things might start to feel cluttered. To address this (and as per user request), there is now an option to ban items from appearing in the game.

To ban an item, simply open its details and click the [i]Ban Item[/i] button.

[h2]Enemy List[/h2]

The collection menu now also displays enemies you’ve defeated at least once:

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45228567/2f88d6f757cbcdacda07960d6f5311e60f0bc9bd.jpg[/img]

You can view their details, including their resistances and the number of times you’ve killed them. Please note that I’ve just started tracking these numbers, so they will initially show zero kills for all enemies. Sorry! (；′⌒`)

[h1]Relics[/h1]

I asked on Discord, and you all seemed fond of the idea of updating the graphics for runes to make them less simplistic. While simple icons are nice, they don’t scale well for other uses.

So now, the runes have been renamed to Relics, complete with a new look:

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45228567/1c3120fcdb6b82a45aa97bc1f923837a0b58b3d0.jpg[/img]

They function the same as before—this is purely a naming and graphical update.

[h1]Relics Synthesizer[/h1]

As requested by one of you, players can now merge relics of the same type and rarity to create more powerful relics:

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45228567/77e9e8623b2cfc9e08b4e33e9e04bb5e4ffbe0c1.jpg[/img]

You’ll need 4 duplicate relics to create one of a higher rarity. The roll value of the new relic will be an average of the roll values of the input relics. A small fee, based on the relic’s rarity, will be required for this process.

You can access the synthesizer via the small menu at the top-right of the relic page.

[h1]Daily Rewards[/h1]

Players will now receive 3 to 5 relics each time they launch the game for the first time that day:

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45228567/354825f9c0d2b614e7272410fe3dc6b55f348340.jpg[/img]

You can inspect the obtained relics directly from this screen by clicking on them:

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45228567/a33fb71ad4b56b4174b8d36f090803644439fc0d.jpg[/img]

[h1]Game Finish Rewards[/h1]

After completing a run, players will now be rewarded 3 to 5 relics (an increase from the flat 3 relics previously). These rewards will appear in the same pop-up as the daily rewards.

On the topic of end-game rewards: runs lasting 30+ minutes in Endless Mode will now count as a victory instead of a loss.

[h1]Component Changes[/h1]

A small but important update: players will no longer be offered components they don’t meet the requirements for.

[h1]New Element[/h1]

Finally, let’s dive into the highlight of this update: a new element! For the first time since the elemental system’s implementation, I'm introducing [b]Dark[/b].

Dark-aligned weapons specialize in high-damage attacks at the cost of health. Each attack drains [b]3 points of health[/b] until 50% of your health is consumed, boosting the weapon’s crit rate by 50%.

Dark element interactions:
[list]
[*] [b]Lightning reaction (Disintegration)[/b] - instantly execute any enemy below 50% health
[*] [b]Light reaction (Nullification) [/b] - Cancels damage from the attack but increases the enemy’s elemental reaction effects by 200% (stackable).
[/list]

[h1]New Weapons[/h1]

There are a total of [b]11[/b] new weapons and [b]1[/b] new item. I’ll leave most of the discoveries to you, but here’s a sneak peek of what’s coming:

• [b]Fireworks [/b]weapon (Unstable, AoE)
• [b]Divine Punishment[/b] weapon (Light, Follow-Up)
• [b]Frost Flames[/b] weapon (Ice, AoE)
• [b]Thundering Slash[/b] weapon (Lightning, Follow-Up)
• [b]Asteroid Belt[/b] weapon (Earth, AoE)
• [b]Dark Projectile[/b] weapon (Dark, Pierce)
• [b]Cursed Slash[/b] weapon (Dark, Simple)
• [b]Devouring Mist[/b] weapon (Dark, DoT)
• [b]Amaterasu[/b] weapon (Dark, AoE)
• [b]Dark Affinity[/b] item (Dark Damage Increase)

[h1]New Locations[/h1]

I don’t usually do this, but here’s a small preview of the new locations:

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45228567/1783ff4fdcf6fb5cf32faaa7d03d63b2451db381.jpg[/img]
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45228567/a7ae891e39eb77089e41e33628196f3012ba775d.jpg[/img]
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45228567/ffccd14b30375e696cc0899e3608cc9b3bc540ba.jpg[/img]
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45228567/59f024a29f239f7c5a06b22008edda3a7329de12.jpg[/img]
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45228567/efbbd8b2aabfb334546885a63691dbcd2d4c663b.jpg[/img]

[h1]Bug fixes and improvements[/h1]

[list]
[*] Fixed [b]Cosmic Affinity[/b] upgrades being replaced by Ice Affinity upgrades
[*] Fixed [b]Wind Affinity[/b] missing upgrades
[*] Fixed [b]Time Blade[/b] weapon's behavior
[*] Fixed a game freeze when skipping a level-up after picking up a big magnet.
[*] Fixed vulnerability application on multiple weapons.
[/list]

[hr][/hr]

That’s it for this update!

I know some promised features haven’t been implemented [i]just yet[/i]—most notably the new character, which I’m still working out the details for. (´。＿。｀)

I’ve also been experimenting with a new map generation system, and it’s showing a lot of promise, though I can’t make any guarantees about when it might be ready.
